question: Does a placebo still work when the patient is told plainly that it is a sugar pill?
answer: In some trials, yes. In a 2010 Harvard study, 80 people with irritable bowel syndrome got nothing, or pills from a bottle labelled placebo. After three weeks, 59% of pill-takers reported adequate relief against 35% of the others. The twice-daily ritual did work once credited to deception.
